labels.label: T-abs-hoist-time-function/has-time-function
labels.notes: HEAD CBG/Pgcd.lean:133-134 is cmp-identical to CurvesExtend.lean:516-517. Causal.Causality.HasTimeFunction keeps its full name, universe list [u_1], type, telescope and value hash. Only its module changed (CBG.Pgcd -> CurvesExtend). The closer rewrote the docstring to correct a library claim. The old text said HasTimeFunction 'is weaker than' IsTimeFunction, and that is false. The doubled line has an ETT time function and is not causal (Causal.exists_isTimeFunction_not_isCausal), while HasTimeFunction implies IsCausal (the new wrapper). The other direction fails at the level of a given T. A constant T on a causality whose <= is equality satisfies the HasTimeFunction body but is not an open map. If x << x is possible, T cannot be strictly increasing along <<. So the new 'neither ... nor' is true, and the references it cites exist: Morphism.lean:832, Cauchy.lean:83, CBG.Dev.causality_hasTimeFunction, kb/0058. Every user still resolves it: Pgcd, Maximal, NoCorresponding, Flat.CBG and EAlphaCauchy all build.

labels.label: T-abs-hoist-time-function/wrappers
labels.notes: Both are new and are the only new public constants. The elaborated types: `Causality.HasTimeFunction.isCausal : ∀ {M : Type u} [TopologicalSpace M] {C : Causality M}, C.HasTimeFunction → C.IsCausal`, and the same for `.curvesExtend` with `C.CurvesExtend`. Neither takes any other hypothesis, instance or separation axiom. isCausal is proved directly. From x ≤ y and y ≤ x, assuming x ≠ y gives T x < T y < T x. This is IsCausal's definition (∀ x y, le ⊤ x y → le ⊤ y x → x = y), and the statement equals isCausal_of_exists_timeFunction read through the predicate (checked by a probe). curvesExtend is curvesExtend_of_timeFunction applied to the two components. The axioms are [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Both sit in an ETT-layer module, so the keeper's concurrent witness switch in programme/ladder.toml (:468, :485) is consistent, and ladder.py check is green.
